sources_considered.why: Original arithmetic and operation-inference experiments cover GPT-J and GPT-Neo models.
Contemporaneous abstract-reasoning study includes both failures and human-like successes.
The 2024 evaluation does not directly establish the state described in February 2023.

evidence_items.locator: Section 4, Summary; arithmetic and operation-inference results
evidence_items.explanation: Experiments on GPT-J and two GPT-Neo sizes find errors in arithmetic and strong dependence on training-term frequency. That supports elementary errors and fragile transfer, although frequency dependence alone does not prove an absence of reasoning.

The study tests 7-billion- and 70-billion-parameter models on three reasoning tasks and finds sensitivity to whether content is familiar or abstract. It also finds above-chance ability and similarities to human errors, which qualify any inference that the models cannot abstract at all.

unresolved_gaps: The studies do not provide a population-wide percentage of LLMs with abstraction problems.
They do not establish that all such errors differ fundamentally from human reasoning errors.
